key_insight: A foundation-model-based temporal scorer can pick the best ultrasound frame for ONSD measurement using sparse supervision and soft temporal labels.
clinical_relevance: This could make optic nerve sheath diameter assessment more accessible in low-resource settings by reducing the expertise needed to choose a usable frame.
method: Ultrasound foundation model embeddings were fed into a lightweight temporal head.
Training used Gaussian soft labels around labeled key frames instead of hard per-frame labels.
Top-k frame selection was used to compare the model with training-free and hard-label baselines.
evidence_signal: In subject-level cross-validation on 18 subjects and 323 videos across nine sweep types, the method identified an optimal frame in 82.2% of evaluated sweeps.
watch_item: Performance was evaluated on a relatively small dataset, so broader validation is needed before real-world deployment.
paper_title: Soft Temporal Scoring Using a Foundation Model: Optimal Frame Selection for Improved ONSD Measurement in Ultrasound Videos
